title: Burst Balloons
prompt:
Balloons have values `nums`. Bursting balloon `i` earns `nums[left] * nums[i] * nums[right]` where left/right are its current neighbors (missing neighbors count as 1). Return the max coins from bursting all balloons.

**Example**: `[3,1,5,8]` → `167`.

Interval DP — but think of the balloon burst **last** in each range, so its neighbors are the fixed range boundaries.
hints: Pad the array with 1 on both ends so edge balloons have neighbors.
dp[left][right] = max coins from bursting all balloons strictly between left and right.
Pick the balloon k burst LAST in (left, right): its gain is `pad[left]*pad[k]*pad[right]` plus the two sub-intervals dp[left][k] and dp[k][right].

solution.explanation: Choosing which balloon to burst FIRST is hard because it changes everyone's neighbors. Reversing it — which balloon in a range is burst LAST — fixes that balloon's neighbors to the untouched range boundaries, decoupling the two sub-ranges into independent subproblems. O(n³) over all intervals and split points.
